reasons: intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played all four cards: Bang Bang! spending the 2 Sparks, then both Kaboom! cards at Shrinker Beetle, then Duck and Cover. This deals 24 printed damage and gains 5 Block, leaving Shrinker Beetle at 16 HP.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered playing both Kaboom! cards and Duck and Cover while saving the 2 Sparks. That line would deal 14 damage, gain 5 Block, and preserve the Spark bank, but it gives up the 10 damage from Bang Bang! with no current-turn benefit from keeping the Sparks.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The chosen line gave up the 2 Sparks and all 3 Energy. The main real cost is spending the Spark bank; if Sparks persist, this removes a future resource. It also leaves no cards unplayed, but none of the unplayed alternatives would have provided a better response to the telegraphed debuff.
answers.q4_different_intent: No. A different enemy intent would not have changed the line. The chosen line already plays the only Block card and all affordable damage. An Attack intent would make the 5 Block more relevant, but it would not make saving Sparks or skipping damage preferable; a Debuff or Strategic intent does not create a reason to hold back either.

survives_means: not yet falsified -- this funnel refuses turns and never rates them

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
